title: HACK-7 PORTCULLIS: The PQC Firewall — a Deterministic Crypto Gate Attacked by Its Own Preregistered Battery (8/8 PASS; PQC Adversarial Series #7)
description:
HACK-7 PORTCULLIS — the PQC Firewall, falsified before sale. After the 30/30 declassified-playbook sweep (HACK-1..6), this battery is the first in the series that attacks a DEFENSIVE PRODUCT rather than the operating perimeter: a standing, fleet-wide post-quantum firewall implemented as a deterministic crypto gate.

Enforcement contract (frozen before the run): single crossing (all crypto-touching operations route through one gate); frozen exact-match allowlist containing ONLY CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, kyber_1024, SPHINCS+-256f (runtime mutation refused); fail-closed on gate silence; recompute-never-trust key validation against registered known-answer vectors; journaled crossings with nonce and freshness binding (replayed authorizations refused); zero LLM in the decision path.

Result: 8/8 preregistered verdicts, 8/8 falsifier checks. Classical downgrade REJECTED; hybrid downgrade (classical-only effective key) REJECTED; weaker PQC variant (Dilithium2) REJECTED by exact-match allowlist; key substitution DETECTED by recomputation; retired-keyset resurrection FAILED CLOSED for a human (resolved under owner ACK through the frozen gate path, single-trust confirmed); positive control ADMITTED (the gate proves it does not false-block legitimate crypto); replayed authorization REFUSED; in-band allowlist tamper REFUSED with the allowlist hash unchanged; gate silence produced NO execution (fail-closed). Two consecutive runs byte-identical (determinism). Zero governance touch (H-INV-1).

Honesty receipt: three harness/fixture authoring defects were caught before any claim — the gate itself refused a mis-keyed fixture — and all are disclosed in the runlog; the passing battery is attempt 4. Preregistration (manifest sha256 49218b4b...45f23a98a) was committed before execution and never edited after freeze.
